paper_metadata.title: Gravitational wave matched filtering by quantum Monte Carlo integration and quantum amplitude amplification

summary: The paper proposes a gate‑based quantum algorithm for gravitational‑wave matched filtering that replaces FFT‑based SNR evaluation with quantum Monte Carlo integration combined with quantum amplitude amplification. The algorithm achieves query complexity ~O(M / √r(ρ_hard)) (or O(M√Ntemp) in the worst case) while reducing qubit requirements from O(M) in FFT‑based approaches to O(poly(log M)) qubits, at the cost of requiring QRAM for detector data loading.

experiments.description: Theoretical gate-based quantum algorithm for gravitational-wave matched filtering using quantum Monte Carlo integration for SNR estimation and quantum amplitude amplification to search over templates and coalescence times.

algorithm.variant: Quantum Monte Carlo integration (QMCI) subroutine combined with quantum amplitude amplification (QAA) for matched filtering

problem_formulation.encoding_details: Template index m and coalescence-time index j are amplitude-encoded in uniform superposition; frequency-bin data are loaded via qRAM into registers for QMCI-based mean estimation.
problem_formulation.objective_function: Determine whether there exists (m,j) such that rho_{m,j} >= threshold, and find one such pair; rho_{m,j} is the matched-filter SNR defined as a mean over frequency bins.
problem_formulation.constraints_handling: Two-threshold scheme: templates with true SNR >= rho_hard should be detected with high probability; templates with true SNR < rho_soft should be rejected with certainty; intermediate region [rho_soft, rho_hard) may be either.

problem_instance.description: Gravitational-wave matched filtering over a template bank and discrete time-of-coalescence grid.

dataset_specification.description: Detector output s(t) / Fourier data \u007es(f_k) and noise PSD S_n(f); gravitational-wave templates \u007eQ_m(f).

problem_instance.data_preprocessing_details: Fourier transform of detector output; normalization of templates; use of one-sided PSD; qRAM loading of real and imaginary parts of \u007es(f_k)/S_n(f_k).
problem_instance.evaluation_methodology: Theoretical complexity analysis only; no numerical experiments or hardware runs reported.

implementation_details.classical_preprocessing: Construct O_Re and O_Im from arithmetic oracles and qRAM-loaded detector data; build O_rho and O_mean oracles; use median-of-means style repetition inside QMCI.
implementation_details.classical_postprocessing: After QAA, measure template/time registers and classically recompute rho_{m,j} to confirm rho_{m,j} >= rho_soft.

results.unit: dimensionless; minimum reported in studied parameter space
dimensionless; maximum reported in studied parameter space

speedup_claims.factor: quadratic speedup over classical exhaustive search in template number
speedup_claims.baseline_method: classical exhaustive matched filtering / exhaustive template search
speedup_claims.conditions: when r(rho_hard) > 0 and under the two-threshold scheme
speedup_claims.caveats: Speedup is asymptotic and assumes fault-tolerant gate-based quantum computing plus qRAM and arithmetic oracles.

speedup_claims.factor: same asymptotic order in M as FFT-based method, but with exponential qubit reduction from O(M) to O(poly(log M))
speedup_claims.conditions: for the QMCI-based SNR estimation subroutine
speedup_claims.caveats: The paper emphasizes qubit savings rather than a better M-scaling in query complexity.

speedup_claims.factor: O(M / sqrt(r(rho_hard))) up to logarithmic factors
speedup_claims.baseline_method: classical O(M log M / r(rho_th)) exhaustive matched filtering
speedup_claims.caveats: This is a query-complexity claim, not an empirical benchmark.

speedup_claims.factor: O(M * sqrt(Ntemp)) up to logarithmic factors in the no-signal worst case
speedup_claims.caveats: Still quadratic in Ntemp relative to classical exhaustive search.

complexity_analysis.quantum_complexity: O(M / sqrt(r(rho_hard))) up to logarithmic factors for the main search; O(M * sqrt(Ntemp)) in the no-signal worst case, up to logarithmic factors
complexity_analysis.classical_complexity: O(Ntemp * M log M) in the exhaustive-search case; O(M log M / r(rho_th)) when a fraction r(rho_th) of templates exceed threshold

advantage_assessment.crossover_size: Not specified; depends on template count Ntemp and time samples M
advantage_assessment.resources_for_advantage: Fault‑tolerant gate-based quantum computer with poly(log M) logical qubits, QRAM capable of loading O(M) detector data, and repeated QMCI/QAA oracle calls scaling as O(M / sqrt(r(ρ_hard))) up to logarithmic factors.
limiting_factors: Large constant factors from QMCI and arithmetic oracle construction
Requirement of QRAM for frequency-bin data access
Need for many logical qubits with error correction
No empirical demonstration or resource estimate in physical qubits

notes: This is a theoretical algorithm paper; no physical QPU, simulator, or experimental run is reported.
The paper explicitly states the qubit scaling in Eq. (39) and the query complexity in Eqs. (40)-(42).
Authors explicitly present only theoretical complexity results and do not run the algorithm on hardware or simulators.
The paper claims quadratic speedup in template search complexity relative to classical exhaustive matched filtering.
